Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:10:2.hebrew: משלם נזק שלם - כסומכוס מוקמינן לה בב"ק, דאמר: בהמה שהזיקה בצרורות, משלם נזק שלם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:10:2.english: Pays full damage - We establish it in Bava Kamma in accordance with Sumkhos, who said: An animal that caused damage through pebbles, [its owner] pays full damage.

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:10:3.english: And they broke the vessels - With their sound.

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:10:4.hebrew: חצי נזק - כדין צרורות, לרבנן דפליגי עליה דסומכוס בב"ק, ואמרי: אינו משלם אלא חצי נזק צרורות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:10:4.english: Half the damage - In accordance with the law of pebbles [tzerorot], according to the Rabbis who disagree with Sumkhus in Bava Kamma and say [that] one pays only half-damage for pebbles.

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:11:1.hebrew: שאני אדם דבר דעת הוא - האי ניזק, וכי מיבעית — מדעתיה קא מיבעית, שנותן לבו אל פחד קול הבא פתאום:
Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:11:1.english: A person is different, as he is mentally competent - [This refers to] this injured party; and when he is frightened, it is of his own mind that he is frightened, as he takes to heart the fright of a sound that comes suddenly.

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:12:1.hebrew: וכהתה - ולא נסמית לגמרי, שרואה במקצת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:12:1.english: And weakened - And it was not completely blinded, for he sees somewhat:

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:12:2.english: If he can make use - With this vision.

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:13:1.hebrew: וצריכי - הני תרתי יצא לחירות לאשמועינן: דהיכא דאין יכול להשתמש, אע"ג דלא סמאה לגמרי — הויא השחתה; והיכא דסמאה לגמרי, אע"ג דכהויה הויא מעיקרא, הואיל והיה יכול להשתמש למראיתה בדוחק — הויא השחתה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:13:1.english: And [both are] necessary - [These two rulings of] "he is emancipated" [are necessary] to teach us: that where he is unable to use [it], even though he did not blind it completely, it is [considered] destruction; and where he blinded it completely, even though it was weak from the outset, since he was able to use its sight with difficulty, it is [considered] destruction.

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:13:2.english: And now [his] vision is weak - That he cannot make use [of it].

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:13:3.hebrew: דמעיקרא נמי נהורא כחישא - ואע"ג דיכול להשתמש בו, אימא לאו עין הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:13:3.english: Where at the outset his vision was also weak - And even though he is able to use it, say that it is not an eye.

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:15:1.english: To drill his tooth - To hollow it out and scrape around its base.

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:16:1.hebrew: לכדתניא הושיט ידו למעי שפחה - להוציא עוברה — פטור, דלא נתכוין לעין כלל. אבל ״כחול לי עיני״, דנתכוין לעין — אע"ג שלא נתכוין לשחתה — חייב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:16:1.english: For that which is taught: He stuck his hand into the womb of a maidservant - [In order] to extract her fetus — he is exempt [from freeing him], as he did not intend [to touch] the eye at all. But [in the case of] “Paint my eye,” where he intended [to treat] the eye, even though he did not intend to destroy it, he is liable [to free him].

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:17:1.hebrew: מושחת - נפקא לן הא דר"א, פרט לזה שלא נתכוין לשחת כלל. ושחתה משמע: בעסוק בה הכתוב מדבר, ואפ"ה מתכוין לשחתה בעינן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:17:1.english: From “and destroys” - We derive this [ruling] of Rabbi Elazar, to exclude this [case, where one] did not intend to destroy at all; and “destroys it” implies [that] the verse speaks of [one who is] engaged with it, and even so, we require [that he] intend to destroy it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:18:1.english: And scooped it out - He removed it to the outside.

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:19:1.hebrew: ותנא תונא - כלומר, מצינו תנא שלנו המסייענו בזאת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:19:1.english: And the Tanna taught - That is to say, we have found a Tanna of ours who supports us in this.

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:19:2.hebrew: ואין תמות וזכרות בעופות - האי קרא דריש הנאמר בכל (כלל) הקרבנות (ויקרא כ״ב:י״ח): "איש איש מבית ישראל אשר יקריב קרבנו לכל נדריהם וגו' לרצונכם תמים זכר בבקר בכשבים ובעזים". מדלא כתיב "לרצונכם זכר תמים" ולישתוק, לימדך שאין מקפיד על תמות וזכרות אלא על אלו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:19:2.english: And unblemished status and male status do not [apply] to birds - [The tanna] expounds this verse that is stated regarding all [the general category of] sacrifices (Leviticus 22:18): "Any man of the house of Israel... who brings his offering for all their vows... for your acceptance, unblemished, a male, among the cattle, among the sheep, or among the goats." Since it is not written: "for your acceptance, a male, unblemished," and stopped there, [this] teaches you that [the Torah] insists upon unblemished status and male status only for these.

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:1:1.hebrew: שן דחלב - שן שינק בה, דעתיד להחליפה, כגון בעבד קטן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:1:1.english: A milk tooth - A tooth with which he nursed, which he is destined to replace, such as in [the case of] a minor slave.

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:20:1.hebrew: נחטטה עינה - אלמא אף על גב דסמויה מעיקרא, כי חטטה משוי ליה מומא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:20:1.english: Its eye was gouged out - Evidently, even though it was blind beforehand, when [one] gouged it out, it renders it a blemish.

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:3:1.hebrew: לחפשי ישלחנו - ריבה לו שלוחים, מדלא כתיב ״חפשי הוא״ או ״יצא חפשי״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:3:1.english: To freedom shall he send him - [Scripture] multiplied releases for him, since it is not written: “He is free” or “He shall go out free.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:4:1.hebrew: בטל ממלאכתו - העין נסמת מראות, והשן מללעוס:
Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:4:1.english: Disabled from its function - The eye is blinded from seeing, and the tooth from chewing.

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:4:2.hebrew: ודילדל בו עצם - השמיטו ממקומו, ומחובר בבשר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:4:2.english: And dislocated a bone in it - He dislodged it from its place, and [it remains] attached by the flesh.

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:4:3.hebrew: יוצא בו לחירות - אם עצם שאינו חוזר הוא, וסופו ליבש וליפול. ואע"ג דליכא ביטול מלאכה — דהא עצם דזקן לאו מידי הוי עביד — כיון דבגלוי הוא ואינו חוזר, הרי הוא כעשרים וארבעה ראשי אברים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:4:3.english: Goes free on account of it - [This applies] if it is a bone that does not regenerate, and is destined to dry up and fall off. And even though there is no cessation of function — for the bone of the beard does not perform any [work] — since it is exposed and does not regenerate, it is like the twenty-four limb tips:

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:4:4.hebrew: ריבויא הוא - אינו לשון כלל להיות נידון בכלל ופרט, אלא בריבה ומיעט וריבה, וריבה הכל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:4:4.english: It is an amplification - It is not phrased as a general statement to be evaluated by [the rule of] a general statement and a specific detail, but rather by [the rule of] an amplification, a restriction, and an amplification; and it amplifies [to include] everything.

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:5:2.hebrew: יוצא בו לחירות - אם עצם שאינו חוזר הוא, וסופו ליבש וליפול. ואע"ג דליכא ביטול מלאכה — דהא עצם דזקן לאו מידי הוי עביד — כיון דבגלוי הוא ואינו חוזר, הרי הוא כעשרים וארבעה ראשי אברים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:5:2.english: [The slave] is emancipated by means of it - If it is a bone that will not regenerate, and is destined to dry up and fall out. And even though there is no loss of function — for the bone of the beard does not perform anything — since it is exposed and does not regenerate, it is like the twenty-four limb extremities.

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:5:3.hebrew: א"כ - דלא ממעט מידי, מיעוט דשן ועין למאי מיעט:
Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:5:3.english: If so - That it excludes nothing — what did the exclusion of tooth and eye come to exclude?

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:6:1.english: With regard to all of them - It refers to the extremities.

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:6:2.english: And requires a bill of manumission - To permit him [to marry] a free woman:

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:7:1.english: Since the Torah granted him [emancipation] - For it is written explicitly.

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:8:1.english: If “freedom” were written at the end, [it would be] as you said - For his emancipation [would be] only through sending [him] away.

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:8:2.hebrew: השתא דכתיב לחפשי ישלחנו הוה ליה חפשי מעיקרא - וכי אתא ישלחנו, לשאר ראשי אברים אתא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:8:2.english: Now that it is written, “To freedom shall he send him,” he is free from the beginning - And when “he shall send him” comes, it comes for the other extremities.

Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:9:1.hebrew: כנגד עינו - שהכה בכותל והבעיתו בקול, ואינו רואה או נתחרש:
Rashi on Kiddushin 24b:9:1.english: Near his eye - Where he struck the wall and startled him with the sound, and [now] he cannot see or became deaf.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 24b:10:1.hebrew: תרנגול שהושיט ראשו וכו' - בתרנגול גרסינן "נזק שלם", ובסוס שצנף — "חצי נזק". וכן מוכח בפרק כיצד הרגל (ב"ק דף יח:):
Tosafot on Kiddushin 24b:10:1.english: "A rooster that stuck its head, etc." - With regard to the rooster, our reading is "full damage," and with regard to a horse that neighed, "half damage." And so it is proven in the chapter [entitled] Keitzad HaRegel (Bava Kamma 18b).

Tosafot on Kiddushin 24b:16:1.hebrew: מיבעי ליה לכדתניא הרי שהושיט כו' - השתא משמע דכ"ע, דכשלא נתכוין לעין — פטור. ותימה, דבפרק כיצד הרגל (ב"ק דף כו:) אמר רבה: היתה מונחת לו אבן בחיקו ולא הכיר בה מעולם, ועמד ונפלה לעין עבד — פלוגתא דרשב"ג ורבנן! וי"ל, דשאני הכא, דאיכא תרתי לטיבותא: שהוא מתכוין לטובה, ולא נתכוין לעין כלל; אבל ההיא דהתם הוי דומיא לכחול לו עין וסמאה, דאיכא חדא לטיבותא — שנתכוין לרפאות, וחדא לריעותא — שנתכוין לעין:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 24b:16:1.english: "[They] require it for that which is taught: If [the master] stuck [his hand]..." etc. - Now it implies that everyone agrees that when he did not intend [to touch] the eye, he is exempt. And this is puzzling, for in the chapter [entitled] Keitzad HaRegel (Bava Kamma 26b), Rabba said: [If] a stone was lying in his lap and he was never aware of it, and he stood up and it fell upon the eye of a slave, [this is subject to] the dispute of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel and the Rabbis! And one can say that here it is different, for there are two favorable factors: that he intends for good, and he did not intend [to touch] the eye at all; but that [case] there is comparable to painting an eye for him and blinding it, where there is one favorable factor — that he intended to heal, and one detrimental factor — that he intended [to touch] the eye.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 24b:18:1.hebrew: סמויה וחטטה יוצא בהן לחירות - ואע"ג דלעיל אמר: כהויה וסמאה, אם אינו יכול להשתמש בה כבר — אין יוצא בהן לחירות; והכא, כיון דסמויה, משמע שלא היה יכול להשתמש בה כבר — מ"מ הכא שאני, דחטטה עשאו מחוסר אבר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 24b:18:1.english: [If his eye was] blind and he gouged it out, [the slave] is emancipated by means of them - And even though earlier [the Gemara] stated: [If it was] dimmed and he blinded it, if he was not already able to use it, he is not emancipated by means of them; and here, since it was blind, it implies that he was not already able to use it — nevertheless, here it is different, for [by] gouging it out, he made him lack a limb.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 24b:19:1.hebrew: [ותנא תונא כו' - תימה, דלא דמי לעוף: דמתחילה לא היה בו דבר שראוי לפסול בו, דאפילו עינו סמויה בו לא היה פסול; אבל עבד, הרי היה בו מתחילה דבר הראוי לצאת בו. ת"י]:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 24b:19:1.english: [“And the tanna also taught,” etc. - [This is] puzzling, as it is not comparable to a bird: For initially, there was nothing in it that was fit to disqualify it, as even if its eye was blind, it was not disqualified; whereas [with] a slave, behold, initially he had something through which he was eligible to go free. — Tosafot Yeshanim]:

Tosafot on Kiddushin 24b:20:1.hebrew: ת"ל מן העוף ולא כל העוף - תימה: ל"ל קרא? כיון דמחוסר אבר פסול לבני נח, כדדרשינן בפ"ק דע"ז (דף ה:) ובפ"ב דזבחים (ד' קטז.): "מכל החי מכל בשר" — הבא בהמה שחיין ראשי אברין שלה! וי"ל: דאי לא כתב קרא גבי ישראל, הוה מוקמינן קרא דבני נח בישראל ולא לבני נח, כדאמר בפרק ד' מיתות (סנהדרין דף נט.): "כל מצוה שנאמרה לבני נח ולא נשנית בסיני — לישראל נאמרה ולא לבני נח". א"נ, ה"א: כיון דאישתרי בעל מום בעופות טפי מבהמה, אישתרי אפילו מחוסר אבר, וקרא דכתיב איירי בבהמה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 24b:20:1.english: "The verse states: 'From the fowl' — and not all fowl" - [This is] puzzling: Why do I need a verse? Since [a creature] lacking a limb is disqualified for descendants of Noah, as we expound in the first chapter of Avodah Zarah (5b) and in the second chapter of Zevachim (116a): "'Of every living thing of all flesh' [Genesis 6:19] — bring an animal whose limb extremities are alive!" And one can say: For had the verse not been written regarding an Israelite, we would have applied the verse regarding the descendants of Noah to Israelites and not to descendants of Noah, as it says in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 59a): "Any mitzvah that was stated to the descendants of Noah and was not repeated at Sinai was stated to Israelites and not to descendants of Noah." Alternatively, one might have said: Since a blemished [creature] is permitted in [the case of] fowl more than [in the case of] an animal, [perhaps] even [a bird] lacking a limb would be permitted, and the verse that is written deals with an animal.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 24b:7:1.hebrew: הואיל ומדרש חכמים הוא - פי': משום הכי אמר דבשאר דברים צריך גט שחרור. וא"ת: ומה בכך הואיל ומדרש חכמים הוא, והלא כמה גופי תורה תלויין שאינם באין אלא מכח דרשה? לכן נראה לר"ת דגט זה אינו אלא מדרבנן, דחיישינן שמא ימצאנו בשוק ויאמר לו: "עבדי אתה", לפי שאין המדרש ידוע לעולם; לכך תקנו גט שחרור. וריב"א פירש דודאי שן ועין, דכתיב בהדיא בקרא ועלייהו כתיב "לחפשי ישלחנו", דמשמע חפשי מעיקרא — ובהא פשיטא ליה דלא גמר "שילוח" "שילוח" מאשה, ולכן א"צ גט שחרור; אבל שאר אברים, דלא נפקי אלא מיתורא דישלחנו, ודאי בהכי גמירי "שילוח" "שילוח" מאשה, ולכך צריך להו גט שחרור:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 24b:7:1.english: "Since it is an interpretation of the Sages" - Explanation: It is on this account that [the arbiter] said that for other matters [i.e., other limbs], he requires a bill of manumission. And if you say: What does it matter that it is an interpretation of the Sages? Are there not many essential Torah laws that hang [without explicit scriptural mention], which are derived only by virtue of an exposition? Therefore, it appears to Rabbeinu Tam that this bill [of manumission] is only rabbinic, for we are concerned lest [the master] find him in the marketplace and say to him, "You are my slave," because the exposition is not known to the public; therefore, they instituted a bill of manumission. And Riva explained that certainly regarding a tooth and an eye, which are written explicitly in the verse and concerning which it is written, "to freedom shall he send him," which implies [that he becomes] free from the start — and in this [case] it is obvious to him that he does not derive [the verbal analogy of] "sending" [and] "sending" from a woman, and therefore he does not require a bill of manumission. But regarding other limbs, which are derived only from the superfluity of "he shall send him" — certainly in that case they learned [the verbal analogy of] "sending" [and] "sending" from a woman, and therefore for them he requires a bill of manumission.
